title: Rabbi Abba, Brother of Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevadi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Yevamot 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83b.9), Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah cites Rabbi Abba, brother of Zevadi, who transmits it in the name of Rav Yehudah, who cites Rav. Hyman cites [Tosafot on 83a, under Rabbi Yose](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Yevamot.83a.9.2) for a reading in which he spoke in Rav Huna’s name. Hyman agrees with that reading: [Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.5.11), 12b, has Rav Huna instructing Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevadi’s brother. It is very unlikely that he is Rabbi Abba bar Zevada: a scholar well known throughout the Talmud would not be identified through a brother mentioned only rarely.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Bavli gives the full brother’s name, Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevadi. Hyman abbreviates it within the quoted chain.

The linked Tosafot gives Rav Huna transmitting in Rav’s name while discussing a ruling about Rabbi Yose. The Jerusalem Talmud names the brother as Rav Huna’s addressee without giving his personal name. [Heilprin’s Abba bar Zavda entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=42&lang=en) includes the Yevamot citation and treats the figures together, an identification Hyman considers very unlikely.
